To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the degree to which a participant is engaged in a citizen science project influences their motivations, which can be deconstructed into three interacting components of interest, action, and situational identity.
the motivations of participants to join and remain engaged in an environmental citizen scientist program evolve over time.

1) the more people participate in an environmental citizen-science program, the more they become invested in it and the science it produces; and 2) the more people become invested in the environmental citizen-science, the more their identity becomes tied to the program and its science.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the motivations of participants in a citizen science program are influenced by their level of participation.
the question of how people’s interests and sense of self evolve as a result of participating in an environmental citizen scientist program.
the motivations of adults in environmental citizen science and the degree to which their engagement, measured as the time they have been in the program, influences their motivations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the study results show that hands-on, adult environmental citizen science programs should focus on contextualizing data collector roles and project design to support both the altruism and self-interest motivations of participants.
citizen science programs should be designed with an eye to the motivations of participants and should evolve to support those motivations over time.

environmental citizen science programs that provide participants with opportunities for meaningful interactions with nature and with others, that are focused on the local environment, and that provide participants with a sense of purpose, can be successful in recruiting and retaining participants and can contribute to the development of a sense of environmental stewardship and identity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
citizen science programs should consider the motivations of participants and design their programs accordingly.
citizen science programs should consider the motivations of their target audience and design their programs accordingly.
the more a person is involved in a program, the more they identify as a citizen scientist.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the more people are exposed to the scientific process, the more likely they are to see themselves as scientists, which in turn, can lead them to become more active in the scientific community and in the conservation of the environment.
the more people become immersed in citizen science programs, the more their interests and identities align with the program.
the sense of self that develops over time is a key driver in the evolution of interest and motivation to remain engaged in environmental citizen science.
